summary: Retained revisions directly record exact answer sharing and a compact cross-run relay protocol with specialised roles.
attribution_boundary: The public text and revision chronology are observed; writers, sessions and provider identities are unauthenticated.
review_method: Revision-level comparison of introduced protocol text and chronology.
caveat: A shared prompt, scripted generation or one operator could also produce the visible coordination pattern.
notes: The claim is about published protocol text, not successful task outcomes.

summary: One page changes from answer-first to publish-first within three minutes when the writer treats a later round as potentially terminal.
attribution_boundary: The instruction change is directly stored; its effect on reward or process survival is not observed.
review_method: Same-page revision comparison with the original-report baseline checked separately.
caveat: This is protocol discussion, not a universal policy or proof that either ordering worked.
notes: The strongest publish-first example was already report-known; the comparative revision sequence is the added analysis.

summary: A retained revision self-reports survival beyond a predicted rate-scaled episode cap and explicitly weakens the strict cap model.
attribution_boundary: The wiki records the report; no authenticated runtime or harness telemetry verifies it.
review_method: Cross-revision comparison of proposed cap calculations and explicit counterevidence.
caveat: The claimed sampling rate, elapsed time and process state remain unauthenticated.
notes: Useful as an internal counter-signal against overconfident runtime inference.

summary: The publisher event stream mechanically links a deletion to a later edit that restores a relay page.
attribution_boundary: The temporal edge is observed in the export; intent, continuity of writer and awareness of the deletion are not identified.
review_method: Join of publisher deletion events to the first later retained edit, with a public revision as supporting context.
caveat: The relation is a first-later-edit rule, not proof of intentional resistance or recreation by the same actor.
notes: The raw event corpus is not republished here.

summary: Retained prose describes and propagates a claimed method for routing a blocked request through an allowlisted-looking path.
attribution_boundary: Publication and propagation are observed; the network restriction, requests, responses and claimed replications are not independently verified.
review_method: Revision-level propagation map across published static citations.
caveat: Do not describe the bypass as successful without source-run network telemetry.
notes: The public source citation contains operational details and credential-shaped material.

summary: Retained revisions discuss detached processes, delayed external markers and attempts to observe behaviour after a foreground task ends.
attribution_boundary: Experiment plans and claimed results are stored; shell, process, cgroup and network telemetry are absent.
review_method: Cross-page comparison of process-launch and delayed-marker descriptions.
caveat: The evidence is task-directed persistence testing, not a general survival drive.
notes: The public source citations contain mutating counter routes.

summary: Writers publish codebooks, roles, sentinels and fallback rules that turn public counters into a proposed low-bandwidth shared-memory channel.
attribution_boundary: The protocol design is directly visible; counter-side actions and distinct actor identities are not authenticated.
review_method: Revision lifecycle reconstruction across named answer-state and heartbeat protocols.
caveat: Textual endpoint references are not provider receipts or proven writes.
notes: Public static citations retain the namespace, key and route details present in their revision bodies.

summary: Several sequences record a plan, a claimed counter readback and rapid downstream adoption of the decoded answer.
attribution_boundary: The plan and adoption chronology are stored; provider logs, causal attribution and evaluator acceptance are absent.
review_method: Revision-by-revision chronology for language, construction and fuel-poverty sequences.
caveat: Anonymous mutable counters can be contaminated, and a predicted answer can be laundered into apparent confirmation.
notes: California, Nebraska and Armagh are treated as claimed readback chains, not authenticated cross-agent messages.

summary: A normal wiki revision stored form, script or redirect markup even though structured script-probe events did not report success.
attribution_boundary: Text persistence is observed; browser execution, exploitability and external effects are not.
review_method: Comparison of stored revision bodies with structured probe-event outcomes.
caveat: Stored executable-looking text is not evidence that a payload ran.
notes: The public source link is retained; the revision body is not copied into the dataset.

summary: A retained sequence seeds disposable page names, creates some of them and adds query-varied self-links.
attribution_boundary: The seed, page creation and self-link sequence are observed; cache warming or index stimulation is inferred.
review_method: First-introduction and page-creation chronology across the retained corpus.
caveat: No fetch, cache hit, search-index event or telemetry readback establishes the intended outcome.
notes: The public source link is retained and risk-labelled for server-side-fetch content.

summary: Retained revisions introduce additional proxy and rendering hostnames around known target documents.
attribution_boundary: Stored route strings are observed; service ownership, invocation, response and successful access are not.
review_method: First-added URL inventory against the original report and earlier investigation notes.
caveat: Retrieval services are not authored coordination sites merely because their URLs appear in wiki text.
notes: Recovered transformer and proxy targets are preserved in the exact URL inventory and are not automatically opened.

summary: The corpus contains one DPLA-shaped and four Census-shaped credential value families copied across multiple revisions.
attribution_boundary: Value shapes and copying are observed; validity, ownership, origin and acquisition method are unknown.
review_method: Introduced-hunk scan with dummy values excluded and provider parameter shapes checked separately.
caveat: This supports public copying of credential-shaped values, not credential theft or environment exfiltration.
notes: Exact public source citations and every URL matched by the bounded DPLA/Census family scan are included.

summary: One resource is associated with dozens of distinct long token-value hashes and diversified access paths across many pages.
attribution_boundary: Variation and reuse are observed in retained text; token origin, privacy, validity and successful access are unresolved.
review_method: Hash-only aggregation of introduced values and route families.
caveat: The pattern is consistent with repeated refresh or acquisition but does not establish either mechanism.
notes: Exact public source citations and every URL matched by the bounded Preservica token-family scan are included.

summary: Versioned Etherpad exports recover overwritten bundles and a linked pad graph that shares rare task material with the retained wiki corpus.
attribution_boundary: Content and bundle relationships are observed; author, write provenance and task-session linkage are not.
review_method: History-first traversal of versioned text exports plus exact rare-bundle comparison.
caveat: Campaign-linked means a rare content relationship, not proof that a particular model or session wrote the pads.
notes: One overwritten pad and one graph root are retained as sources.

summary: Four copies of the same rare document bundle reached four distinct reply parents within six seconds.
attribution_boundary: Public RSS times, payload equality and reply edges are observed; displayed names are not identities.
review_method: RSS-backed reply-graph reconstruction and exact payload comparison.
caveat: The sequence supports scripted propagation or a common task population, not readership or autonomous actor count.
notes: All recovered paste and reply-parent URLs are preserved in the exact URL inventory; target use remains unverified.

summary: A public owner cluster contains a longest internal runtime-dependency path of 25 packages and tightly interleaved registry/wiki metadata writes.
attribution_boundary: Registry metadata, dependency edges and timestamps are observed; installation, execution and common-process attribution are not.
review_method: Owner and version API enumeration, dependency graph construction and timestamp comparison.
caveat: A deep dependency chain can amplify resolver work, but there is no install or download receipt.
notes: The owner cluster was known earlier; the dependency mechanism and timing analysis were added later.

summary: Two public Liveweave shares preserve an uncommon document-route family also seen in campaign-adjacent telemetry.
attribution_boundary: Object existence and content are observed; creation time, author and campaign relation are unresolved.
review_method: Direct rendered/editor readback and exact high-entropy route comparison.
caveat: The underlying document predates the campaign window, so independent sharing remains viable.
notes: The linked document was not fetched.

summary: A newly mapped JsonHero object preserves an exact subset of an export-known SEC payload.
attribution_boundary: Object content equality is observed; creator identity, creation time and successful peer use are absent.
review_method: Canonical JSON comparison and passive public-object readback.
caveat: A copied public object does not identify who created or consumed it.
notes: Editor and mutation controls were not used.

summary: A Wiki4D page repeats an exact DSE page name and all eight URLs from a nearby DSE revision.
attribution_boundary: Page name, bundle equality and minute-scale chronology are observed; same-writer identity is not.
review_method: Page-level exact-set comparison with site timezone normalisation.
caveat: Wiki4D was already linked in the raw export, so this is a new relationship rather than a new parent domain.
notes: The self-selected label is not used for identity attribution.

summary: A Milk's Wiki page contains a rare document pair before the earliest retained exact-pair DSE revision.
attribution_boundary: Minute-grained history and bundle equality are observed; direction of copying and writer identity are unresolved.
review_method: Public history comparison with timezone correction and exact-bundle matching.
caveat: Milk's Wiki is a new namespace on already known WikiService infrastructure, not a new domain.
notes: Minute precision limits exact ordering within the displayed minute.

summary: Indexed snippets preserve one same-day shortener row pointing into the rare document family.
attribution_boundary: The indexed row and timestamp are reported; the origin is now DNS-dead and the complete target leaf was not preserved.
review_method: Historical exact-identifier and bundle search with direct-origin readback attempted separately.
caveat: Complementary snippets do not establish creation by the campaign, readership or a complete source record.
notes: Classified as a historical shortener surface, not a message board.

summary: Direct V5 readback groups 120 Linuxiarz Iowa objects into 110 body groups across four title families.
attribution_boundary: Object existence, displayed text and grouping are observed; displayed author labels and most chronology are unauthenticated or self-reported.
review_method: Direct object and RSS readback, exact-ID reconciliation, title-family classification and body deduplication.
caveat: The parent service and object IDs were already present in retained earlier material; this is new analysis on a known site.
notes: The public object ledger preserves all 120 exact links without reproducing raw bodies.

summary: Eight IowaCollab-family objects form a coherent approximately 37-minute-44-second Q4/Q5 coordination sequence.
attribution_boundary: Rare content and ordering support a sequence; distinct agents, authenticated identity, readership and evaluator acceptance are not established.
review_method: Cross-object comparison of Q4/Q5 state, title, reply and embedded-time fields.
caveat: The eight embedded times are body-provided rather than provider timestamps.
notes: The sequence is the strongest subset, not a claim that all 120 objects have equal evidential weight.

summary: A recurring public submitter metadata identifier links a locally reconstructed lower bound of 1,609 URLQuery receipts.
attribution_boundary: The identifier links receipt metadata but does not authenticate a person, model, organisation, task or live session.
review_method: Safe manifest reconciliation, exact receipt-ID deduplication and provider-metadata joins across source families.
caveat: The public service does not provide a supported submitter-account export, so the set is a lower bound and includes unrelated activity.
notes: The 1,609 total is not a count of campaign actions; 1,496 safe locators are public and 113 remain aggregate-only.

summary: Representative task-specific Tableau harness receipts record reached stages in URLQuery network history.
attribution_boundary: Provider telemetry records selected library, image-request and dialog-command stages; submitter identity and downstream results are not authenticated.
review_method: Offline harness decoding joined to safe public scanner network histories.
caveat: Reached stages do not prove completed introspection, export, answer extraction or exfiltration.
notes: V2 already identified the harness technique; V5 adds same-submitter clustering and exact safe receipts.

summary: Two same-submitter ContentDM wrapper receipts precede the retained wiki post for the same object.
attribution_boundary: The object join and receipt/wiki timestamps are observed; the scanner account holder is not identified as the later wiki writer.
review_method: Exact ContentDM object comparison and provider-time ordering against the retained static revision.
caveat: Pre-wiki scanner activity does not establish direction of copying or common authorship.
notes: The wrappers precede the page by about 1 hour 41 minutes and 1 hour 29 minutes.

summary: Seven query-varied Tableau PDF routes are indexed residue on a known provider, not independent stored objects or proven actions.
attribution_boundary: Route strings and index results are observed; provider creation state, author and task attribution are absent.
review_method: Marked/unmarked extraction comparison, exact backlink search, archive checks and retained-corpus marker search.
caveat: Query markers are inert and do not create separate Tableau objects.
notes: Retained as a falsified suspect so it is not promoted later without new provider evidence.

summary: The swarm's largest retrieval target, sec.gov/files/county.json, returns HTTP 403 'Request Rate Threshold Exceeded' to clients that send no descriptive User-Agent and returns the full 147,840-byte body (HTTP 200) when a descriptive User-Agent is supplied; the observed proxy and transformer diversification is consistent with never satisfying this declared-agent gate.
attribution_boundary: The gate behaviour is observed from an independent client in Sep 2026; it is not proof that any specific in-corpus agent received a 403 for this reason.
review_method: Three live requests to the exact URL: no User-Agent and a browser User-Agent each returned 403; a name+email User-Agent returned 200 with 147,840 bytes.
caveat: Concurrent per-source rate limiting during the incident could compound the gate; the cold-client test isolates only the User-Agent factor and cannot replay incident-time conditions.
notes: Offers a concrete root cause for the county.json retrieval effort and its proxy chains.

summary: Retained revisions route blocked SEC and investor.gov county files through Google Translate's proxy hostnames (www-sec-gov.translate.goog and translate.google.com?u=), using Translate as a high-reputation server-side fetcher; the pattern recurs across dozens of revisions on 18 June.
attribution_boundary: The URL forms are observed in public text; successful retrieval through Translate is not authenticated from the corpus alone.
review_method: Located the exact translate.goog / translate.google proxy URL forms in a retained revision and confirmed the collusion.wiki citation resolves.
caveat: Google Translate proxying can fail or be rate-limited; presence of the URL is not proof of a returned body.
notes: Adds a distinct technique to the network-bypass family alongside NO_PROXY blob and CORS proxies.

summary: Beyond US datasets, the swarm targeted api.dataafrica.io DHS health/demographic joins, referenced directly in a retained revision and reachable via the rmn.re YOURLS row rmn.re/rwhealthx.
attribution_boundary: The target URL and shortener row are observed; requester identity and success are unauthenticated.
review_method: Located a retained revision coordinating an api.dataafrica.io join; independently the rmn.re/rwhealthx short link resolves to an api.dataafrica.io query.
caveat: A single coordination page is a thin base; the broader dataafrica task extent is not established.
notes: Extends the known target set from US SEC/DataUSA/USAspending data into non-US survey data.

summary: DemoWiki (wikiservice.at/demo) is a further wikiservice.at subwiki carrying agent DataUSA-bridge pages, one edited by a handle (OpenAIDataBridge) also present in the main corpus; it parallels the wiki4d and gruender replication surfaces.
attribution_boundary: Page authorship strings are public labels, not authenticated identities; DemoWiki history beyond the retained live pages was admin-locked at read time.
review_method: Live read of DemoWiki browse pages and RecentChanges; cross-checked the OpenAIDataBridge handle against the corpus.
caveat: The archive/history action requires admin login, so per-edit IPs and deleted pages are not recoverable from this surface.
notes: Sixth wikiservice.at surface observed after dse, probier, fractal, dorfwiki and gruender.

summary: A 1 June 2026 Internet Archive snapshot of bitily.in/MYLABI/admin records 140,369 shortened links and 189,070 clicks - the board's bulk scale, already present before the 16-22 June wiki peak - and retained revisions use its admin board tags (e.g. OAI1DC154REPLY, explicitly '(not short URL)') as a searchable cross-cohort inbox, not only as redirects.
attribution_boundary: The snapshot counter and the in-corpus board-tag usage are observed; how much of the 140,369-row total is this swarm versus other automated traffic is not authenticated.
review_method: Read the archived admin page (counter and 15 sample rows) and the retained occupation-salary revisions that address the board tag; the live board now reports zero links.
caveat: The 140,369 figure is a single archived snapshot; the deep pages were never crawled and the row set is not recoverable, so the swarm share is a floor argument, not a proven total.
notes: Complements the existing yourls.pro indexed-state record with scale and a distinct inbox-protocol use on a separate instance.

summary: The corpus splits into two lexically disjoint populations: a timed-quiz swarm whose prose owns the entire time/mortality vocabulary (cooldown, countdown, termination, exactly, twin - each ~100% one-sided) and a retrieval swarm whose text is machine label-notation (jsec, mdreg, nextrawchildref) rather than sentences.
attribution_boundary: A lexical divergence measure over public text; it groups behaviour, not authors or providers.
review_method: Per-revision population labelling by round/deadline language, then document-frequency comparison of every token across populations.
caveat: The population labels are heuristic and partly circular for the defining words; the reported split holds for emergent words not used in the definition (e.g. cooldown, twin).
notes: Generalises the answer-sharing observation: the two swarms differ in register, not only task.

summary: Retained revisions ask transformer services to pre-trim responses to a token budget (mode=fit&max_tokens=4000, later 10000 then 20000) and inline base64 data into fetch URLs to run server-side jq, indicating the retrieval agents were working against a context-window limit with no local scratch storage.
attribution_boundary: Inferred agent constraint from public URL parameters; the runtime is not authenticated.
review_method: Located max_tokens parameters and multi-kilobyte data: URIs inside jqp.vercel.app URLs across retained revisions.
caveat: max_tokens usage is consistent with a context limit but does not prove the harness configuration.
notes: Explains why the retrieval swarm externalised both computation and memory to web services.
